input.question: Why do some people binge eat when they're stressed, while others lose their appetite entirely?
input.ground_truth: I'm gonna call the genetic variation card here. Eating while you're stressed makes sense for many reasons (additional energy may aid in alleviating the cause of the stress, plus the happiness of eating cancels out the unhappiness left by stress). However the inverse also has it's advantages (i.e, if you're in a sticky situation, thinking about eating may not be the most productive thing to do). Psychological factors may also be at play, including strength of will and how the specific person perceives eating.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do some people binge eat when they're stressed, while others lose their appetite entirely?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have two friends, Sam and Alex.

When Sam feels sad or worried (that's called stress), he wants to eat lots and lots of snacks, like cookies and chips. He eats so much that he can't stop, even if he's not hungry. This is called binge eating.

But Alex, when he feels sad or worried, doesn't want to eat anything at all. He might not even want his favorite sandwich or fruit. He just doesn't feel like eating.

This happens because everyone’s body and brain react to stress in different ways. Some people’s bodies tell them, “Eat more!” when they’re stressed, maybe because food makes them feel better for a little while. Other people’s bodies say, “I don’t want anything to eat,” because stress makes them feel sick or not hungry.

It’s like how some kids want a hug when they’re upset, and some kids want to be left alone. Everyone is different!
